text:
m1 - the vehicle landed (2255628, plus 0835c08 closing its Mirror forge) and site 1 is migrated. Working the remaining sites I found something that is squarely this bead's reason for existing, and I want it ruled before I touch the other four.

THE TWO 0.5 THRESHOLDS DISAGREE ABOUT THE SAME UNIT.

PlacementResolution.clearsThreshold tests RESOLVED MASS - everything not Unresolved - against DefaultAbstentionThreshold 0.5.
ProfileScoring.MembershipThreshold tests MASS ON ONE CLASS against 0.5 (Scoring.scala:365, applied at :394, :483, :545).

Same number, different quantity, and a unit can clear one while failing the other. Demonstrated on the exact masses induction produces for PlacementBasis.Ambiguous (induce.scala:473-477 through dist(): primary Unresolved 0.4, rest 0.6, each candidate 0.6 * 0.5 = 0.3):

  resolved mass 0.6 -> clearsThreshold = TRUE  ("resolved enough, publish the number")
  target mass 0.3   -> not a member
  other mass 0.3    -> not a member
  => the resolution summary says PUBLISH; every membership metric counts the unit in ZERO classes.

So the vehicle certifies a placement as resolved while eventPurity, semanticization, otherEventDrift, redundancy and probeGain have all silently dropped that unit. Sixty percent of its mass is genuinely resolved to episodes - it is not abstention - and it contributes to nothing. This is exactly the "five sites inventing five incompatible ways to express fractional placement" you created the bead to prevent, except it is worse than incompatible: it is two vocabularies that both say 0.5 and mean different things, which is how it survived review.

A SECOND THING I CHECKED AND AM NOT CLAIMING. Membership is `>=`, so two candidates at exactly 0.5 would put one unit in two mutually exclusive classes. NOT REACHABLE through induction: InductionConfig.mass requires every mass in (0, 1] strictly (induce.scala:86), so dist's primary is always > 0, rest is always < 1, and two candidates cannot both reach 0.5. I raise it only because nothing STRUCTURALLY prevents it if a Distribution is ever built another way, and because I would rather show you the check I did than have you wonder whether I did it.

WHAT I THINK THE RULING SHOULD BE, though it is yours. The membership threshold is not wrong - "is this unit in this class" genuinely needs concentrated mass, and a unit split 0.3/0.3 is not confidently in either. What is wrong is that the two failures are recorded identically. A unit that is 0.4 Unresolved and a unit that is 0.6 resolved but split evenly are both absent from the counts, and only the first is a model abstention; the second is a real placement the metric cannot express. Per this bead's own ruled constraint - any conditional ratio travels with its resolution mass - the membership-based CoveredScores should carry a PlacementResolution whose `excluded` arm holds the resolved-but-unconcentrated mass. That keeps the three arms summing to 1 without renormalizing and makes the two failures different objects, which is the same fix that worked for causalPreservation in align an hour ago.

I have NOT implemented it. It changes published profile numbers across six metrics and the right shape is a ruling, not an implementation detail. Probes run and deleted; nothing committed; worktree clean.

Tell me which way and I will do the remaining four sites in one pass.
